ctx.x: So, we have to start somewhere, and I'd like to begin by just laying down perhaps a few factual type things about your early training, about some of your early teachers in New York, and perhaps some of the details what it was you gleaned from their instruction.

Now, in several biographical sketches about you, you mention 2 people in particular quite often; one was a man that you referred to as Mr. Michaels, and another one by the name of Arthur Reeves, and I'm wondering if you could tell us, first of all, about Mr. Michaels. Do you remember his first name?
